sa_market_summary: The Suzuki Swift has quietly become one of South Africa's most popular hatchbacks, consistently ranking in the top 3 best-selling passenger cars. The fourth-generation Swift (2024+) introduced a new 1.2-litre three-cylinder engine (60kW/112Nm) that is lighter and 10% more fuel-efficient than its predecessor. Used Swift sales surged 66% year-on-year in 2026, driven by buyers seeking affordable, reliable transport. The Indian-built Swift undercuts the VW Polo Vivo on price while offering impressive standard safety features including six airbags across all trims. The 5-year/200,000km warranty adds peace of mind. The Swift Sport (1.4T, 103kW) offers warm-hatch performance for enthusiasts.

known_faults.description: Oxygen sensors on the ZC31 generation Swift (2008-2011) are prone to failure, triggering the engine management light. The car will still drive but fuel economy suffers.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Check for any warning lights on the dashboard. Request a diagnostic scan for O2 sensor fault codes.
known_faults.source: Suzuki SA service records, AutoTrader SA buyer guides

known_faults.description: Earlier ZC62 (2011-2017) and ZC63 (2018-2024) Swifts can suffer from body rust, particularly on coastal vehicles. This was addressed from 2021 onwards with improved anti-corrosion treatment.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Check undercarriage, suspension mounting points, and door sills for signs of corrosion. Coastal cars (Durban, Cape Town) are highest risk.
known_faults.estimated_repair_zar: R3,000 - R12,000 (panel repair and rust treatment)
known_faults.source: Suzuki SA technical bulletins, SA body shop reports

known_faults.description: The ZC62 generation (2011-2017) is known for premature clutch wear, particularly in stop-start urban driving. Vehicles around 100,000km may require a new clutch.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Test the clutch bite point ,  if very high, the clutch is worn. Check for slipping in higher gears under load.
known_faults.source: SA Suzuki specialist reports, AutoTrader SA buyer guides

known_faults.description: A June 2025 recall affected 2024 model year Swifts for overheating gearbox fluid. Check by VIN on Suzuki SA's recall portal.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Verify recall status by entering the VIN at suzukiauto.co.za. Confirm the recall work has been completed.
known_faults.source: Suzuki SA recall database, AutoTrader SA

what_to_inspect_before_buying: Check for full Suzuki SA service history ,  skipped services can void the 5-year/200,000km warranty
Inspect for rust on undercarriage and suspension, particularly coastal vehicles
Verify 2024 model year CVT gearbox recall has been completed
Test clutch bite point on manual models ,  high bite indicates wear
Check all electricals ,  window switches, infotainment, air conditioning
Request a diagnostic scan for stored fault codes
Inspect tyre condition and brand ,  good tyres indicate a careful owner
Check the small 37-litre fuel tank is adequate for your driving range needs
owner_sentiment: Very positive. The Suzuki Swift is prized for exceptional fuel economy (real-world 4.5-5.5L/100km), low maintenance costs, and strong reliability. Owners value the standard safety features (six airbags on all trims) and the five-year warranty. The main criticisms are the small 37-litre fuel tank (frequent fill-ups), basic infotainment on GL models, and the lack of automated central locking on entry-level variants. The Swift Sport is loved by enthusiasts but considered pricey for its performance level.
